title: Contractualizer: OpenAI Chat Completions request/response contract mapper
creator: Asha Menon
description: Goal: Implement a robust request/response mapping layer ("Contractualizer") that translates OpenAI Chat Completions (v1/chat/completions style) requests and streaming responses into Redwood's canonical runtime contract and back, preserving semantics for streaming, function/tool calling, and structured outputs. The layer must: 1) accept legacy OA chat payloads from customers who integrated the OpenAI API, 2) map messages, roles, and function_call hints into Redwood request primitives, 3) stream partial tokens/events from the runtime back in an OpenAI-compatible SSE/stream envelope, and 4) surface model function calls and structured output validation errors in a way clients expecting OpenAI behavior can consume. This ticket implements the mapping rules, edge-case heuristics, and a small compatibility shim that sits at our edge gateway before requests hit policy/routing. It is intentionally conservative: prefer lossless mapping where possible and explicit fallbacks when not. Example mapping snippets (pseudo-serialized): - OA request messages -> Redwood messages: "[{\"role\":\"system\",\"content\":\"...\"},{\"role\":\"user\",\"content\":\"...\"}]" maps to Redwood.dialog: [{"speaker":"system","text":"..."},{"speaker":"user","text":"..."}] - OA function_call hint: "function_call": {"name":"search","arguments":"..."} should become a tool_call event in Redwood with tool.name=search and input arguments preserved as a string blob plus an attempt to parse JSON into structured args when JSON-like. - Streaming: OA SSE token fragments containing "delta": {"content":"...","role":"assistant","function_call": {...}} must be correlated to Redwood stream frames that emit token deltas, tool-invocation partials, and an explicit end-of-stream event. Where Redwood emits structured output tokens (e.g., JSON schema emission with separate 'start_schema'/'end_schema' markers), the Contractualizer must reframe them into a single content stream with content-type hints so OA clients can reconstruct the object. Primary success metrics: parity for common OA client SDKs (node, python) when hitting the compatibility endpoint, <0.5% increase in median latency for mapped requests, and no semantic loss in function call delivery for 99.9% of requests.
acceptance_criteria: Compatibility endpoint /v1/oa-cc-proxy accepts OpenAI-style chat create requests and returns semantically equivalent responses from Redwood models
Streaming SSE parity: node/python OA SDKs reconstruct messages and function_call events from our SSE stream without application code changes in representative test apps
Tool/function calls produced by models are delivered to the runtime and result in the same sequence of tool-invocation, tool-result, and assistant-final messages as in native OA flows
Structured-output (JSON-schema) responses are validated; validation failures produce OA-compatible error frames and an explanatory message in assistant content
Telemetry: every mapped request emits an interoperability tag and mapping delta metric (num fields dropped, fallback used) visible in console-interop dashboards
No regressions in Redwood auth/rate-limits or routing logic; integration tests pass against dedicated and hosted runtime variants
design_decisions: Expose a dedicated compatibility path (/v1/oa-cc-proxy) rather than altering core API surface to keep contract mapping isolated
Prefer explicit fallbacks with info-level warnings in assistant content when precise mapping is impossible (e.g., non-JSON function arguments) instead of silent drops
Emit mapping diagnostics as headers (X-Rwd-Compat-Delta) and telemetry events rather than mutating customer-visible tokens unless required
Streaming translation will buffer up to N tokens (configurable, default 16) to reframe Redwood multi-part schema emissions into single OA content chunks to minimize client-side parsing differences
Function call resolution: attempt JSON-parse of function arguments, but preserve raw string as 'raw_arguments' in tool-call payload for later debugging
tradeoffs: Latency vs fidelity: reframing some runtime events into OA-compatible envelopes requires small buffering -> slight added latency (configurable), but avoids breaking client SDKs
Complexity vs maintainability: adding a compatibility layer duplicates some mapping logic; chosen to minimize risk to core runtime and keep opt-in compatibility

Lossiness: Certain Redwood-native structured signals (e.g., typed token metadata) will be flattened into text or headers when sent to OA clients — accepted for now with telemetry so we can prioritize most-used signals
rollout_plan: Alpha (internal): enable for internal dev orgs + Redwood SDK integration tests (2 days)
Beta: opt-in for existing customers via feature flag; collect mapping delta metrics and SDK failure reports (2 weeks)
Gradual GA: enable routing rule for legacy API key prefix with 5% traffic, monitor errors/latency, increase incrementally to 100% for legacy keys if stable
Fallbacks: automatic downgrade to simple passthrough 415/501 responses when model variant does not support tool calls — tracked in telemetry and surfaced in console
test_plan: Unit tests for message role mapping, function_call extraction, and raw-argument preservation
Integration tests simulating OA node/python SDKs performing streaming reads and reconstructing function_call events
Chaos tests: inject partial SSE frames and truncated tool outputs to verify graceful client-visible errors
End-to-end smoke: run compatibility test suite against runtime-1.20 staging and Dedicated config with burst capacity on to validate batching interactions
